rubrics.justification: Accurately describes a good-quality expanded blastocyst with favorable ICM and TE and notes limits of a single still image; minor overreach in mentioning partial zona opening/hatching ambiguity not clearly established.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, smoking, endometrium, cycle history, and semen data well with prognosis, though interaction of male-factor diagnosis versus normal semen parameters could be explored more carefully.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent, linking strong embryo morphology and young age with good prognosis while adjusting downward for smoking and BMI; minor inconsistency around 3AA vs 4AA nomenclature does not materially affect conclusions.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: morphology interpreted appropriately, SET favored in a young patient with a high-quality blastocyst, and smoking cessation emphasized; slight looseness around Gardner stage terminology prevents a perfect score.

Provides practical next steps including proceeding with transfer, smoking cessation, peri-transfer optimization, and SET; useful but future-cycle planning is only partially developed in the visible response.
